name: php-src
one_liner: The actual engine that runs the PHP programming language — the software that powers huge chunks of the web, from WordPress blogs to Facebook's early codebase.
buyer: Nobody buys this directly — it's free, public infrastructure maintained by volunteers and companies like Zend/Perforce. The real 'buyer' is any business that already runs a PHP website and depends on it staying fast and secure.
business_use_cases: A hosting company bundles the latest PHP runtime into its shared-hosting plans so WordPress and Laravel sites run faster and more securely.
A dev agency keeps client PHP sites on a supported PHP version to avoid security liability and stay eligible for extension support.
A performance consultancy profiles a client's e-commerce site against the newest PHP release and sells a 'free speed upgrade' as a paid migration project.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid 'PHP version upgrade & compatibility audit' services to agencies still running old PHP versions on client sites.
Run a managed PHP hosting service that always tracks the latest stable release and markets that as a security/performance selling point.

steal_this: Build a one-click 'is your PHP site safe?' scanner that checks a site's PHP version and flags outdated/unsupported runtimes for small business owners who don't know what PHP even is.
